title: A counterexample to Purdy's inequality for hyperplane arrangements in projective three-space
summary: We record an explicit counterexample to a refined form of Purdy's inequality for essential hyperplane arrangements in projective three-space. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an arrangement of $n$ hyperplanes in $\mathbb{P}^3_{\mathbb{C}}$. Let $\ell$ be the number of distinct intersection lines of $\mathcal{A}$, and let $p$ be the number of intersection points, where an intersection point means a point at which at least three hyperplanes meet.
